correctness.rationale: PASS: for a,b,c>0 three dihedrals are right and the other three are arctan(a/b), arctan(c/b), arccos(ac/(sqrt(a²+b²)sqrt(b²+c²))). Reconstructed face-normal sign convention (interior angle = arccos(-n_i·n_j)), so δ is minimum of those three acute angles. With t<=δ, sin²t<=cos t; equality yields t=acos(1/φ) with a/b=c/b=sqrt(φ), and these values are attainable. For π/4<t<=θ*, sin α sin γ<=cos t yields individual bounds tan t<=a/b,c/b<=cos t/sqrt(sin²t-cos²t), attained with the opposite angle exactly t. For t<=π/4, one ratio diverges with the other angle equal t. This exactly proves open/closed/empty boundary cases, not a numerical optimization. Independent outward-face-normal and trigonometric computations on 2000 random triples plus equality and superlevel samples corroborated.
